chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Keg Johnson: nervous temperament, teacher and section mate
summary: Keg Johnson played better in the dressing room than on stage, inspired others, sent Jackson to teachers in Chicago, and anchored a great Calloway trombone section.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Now, let's get -- What about my best buddy, Keg Johnson?
Keg Johnson. I first knew Keg in Chicago. He was playing around there. He had played with Louie.
Right.
That's when I first heard of Keg. Keg had a phenomenal lip, too.
Yeah, a thin sound but a very --
Well, now, I can't say he had a thin sound. I wouldn't say that about Keg.
Well, you know better.

But I'll tell you something about Keg. Keg, he was like -- he had a nervous temperament inside. A lot of people didn't know that. Because he could play you more things up in the dressing room on the trombone and he would get down on the stage --
Right.
-- and he would start to play something and he would tighten up, --
Right.
-- you see.
He was a teacher. He could inspire and help anybody --
Couldn't he?

-- where they're almost -- I mean, he solely -- I could say almost singlehandedly Keg Johnson was responsible for any improvement I ever made in my life. But I was never able to help him improve because he couldn't accept things like that.
Well, you know, he helped me.
Right. Everybody.

He got me to go to my first teacher I ever went to when I went to Jerry [Chimmer] in Chicago when we was playing in Chicago in 1941. He got me to go to Jerry [Chimmer.] He also got me to go to Donald [Reinhardt.] Keg did this.
But Keg could play a lot of trombone. He could do anything that he wants to do with the horn and he could play anything that you would put up in front of him.
And he was great behind a soloist.
Oh, definitely.
Oh, he could --
Definitely. Definitely.
I think that was his best thing where he would stay in the background and let somebody be singing and he'd just put those little things in behind them. It was always beautiful.
Yeah. Well, you see, because he was not there by himself, you see. That [added] a little thing, too, you know.
Right, right.

He had a beautiful sound to me, and we had a very good section. The section blended. You know, I've never played with a bad trombone section in my whole life and that was one of the great trombone sections, to me, that we had in Calloway's band with Keg and Tyree and myself.
Well, I don't think it could be a bad trombone section if you were in there, anyway. If anybody listened to you in any kind of a way, it couldn't be bad.
[Yeah]
And what about --
Tyree used to tell me he'd like to have me in his left ear.
